Hello! Here you'll find all of the exciting work and research I've been doing in BIO 145! 

![](mudkip.png)

## About Me

Hello! I'm **Dr. George Ni**, and I'm interested in invasive species ecology, and the use of computational approaches to answering management questions. 

Throughout this course, I'll use this website to document my work in **R**, including data visualization, ecological modeling, analysis of published datasets, and my final independent research project.



# Portfolio Directory

## Ecological Modeling

In this section, I explore how computational models can be used to represent ecological processes.

Topics include:

- Exponential population growth
- Logistic population growth
- Predator-prey interactions
- Effects of changing model parameters

[**View my ecological modeling work →**](modeling.html)

---

## Recreating Published Research

One goal of this course is to understand how computational analyses are used in published ecological research.

Here, I work with real datasets from published studies and attempt to reproduce or extend some of their figures and analyses.

[**View my paper replication project →**](paper_replication.html)

---

## Research Interests

I'm especially interested in biological control and the ecology of parasitoids.

One example is my research on the cold tolerance of *Tetrastichus planipennisi*, a parasitoid released as a biological control agent for emerald ash borer.

[**Learn more about this research →**](Tet_Data_Analysis.html)

---

## Independent Research Project

For my final project, I will develop an independent ecological or evolutionary research question using an existing dataset.

This project will include:

- A biological question and hypothesis
- Exploration of a real dataset
- Statistical analysis
- Publication-quality figures
- Interpretation of results
- A mock scientific manuscript formatted for a selected journal

[**View my final research project →**](final_project.html)
